subject: Follow-up: evaluation pack & A/B schedule for rerank validation
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@shopline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: evaluation pack & A/B schedule for rerank validation

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the things we promised to share:

- I attached the prompt set we used for your discovery benchmarks (prompt_set_v2.jsonl).
- We’ll send a short CSV with NDCG/MRR slices for the head/tail buckets — should help prioritize where rerank wins matter most.
- Proposed next step: a two-week A/B canary (5% traffic → 20% → 100%) with automatic rollback on NDCG drop >1.5 pts or MRR regression >3%.

Open asks for your side:
1) Confirm which customer segments you want in the canary (search vs. browse vs. recommendations).
2) Any redlines on the SLA/rollback rules above?

Attachments: prompt_set_v2.jsonl (application/jsonlines)

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---
From: Emily Zhang <emily@shopline.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: evaluation pack & A/B schedule for rerank validation

Sergio —

Thanks, got the prompt set. I pulled a quick evaluation against our in-house holdout and attached the CSV (shopline_rerank_eval_summary.csv). Key takeaways:

- Baseline (current production) NDCG@10 = 0.472, MRR = 0.361
- Redwood-rerank-small (quantized) NDCG@10 = 0.491 (+0.019), MRR = 0.372 (+0.011)
- Redwood-rerank-large NDCG@10 = 0.503 (+0.031), MRR = 0.381 (+0.020)

We do see improvements concentrated in mid-tail (queries with 3–10 candidate items). For head queries (>100 monthly searches) lifts are smaller but still positive.

We want the canary to start on search (desktop + mobile) only. For segments, prioritize US region first; EU can follow.

Two questions from my side:
- Can Redwood run the automatic gating checks on our side (so we can see the real-time dashboard)?
- Timeline: we’re aiming to start the canary week of May 17. Is that realistic?

Attachments: shopline_rerank_eval_summary.csv (text/csv)

Thanks,
Emily Zhang
Product Manager, Search
Shopline

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@shopline.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: evaluation pack & A/B schedule for rerank validation

Emily / team —

Great to see positive lifts in the CSV. A few recommendations from our evaluation team and an ops plan for the canary:

1) Recommended model variants to trial
   - redwood-rerank-small-8bit: best cost/latency tradeoff. Expect ~+0.015 NDCG over baseline in production slices; significantly cheaper token costs.
   - redwood-rerank-large-fp16: max quality path. Expect ~+0.03 NDCG but ~1.8x inference cost.

2) Prompt / inference config
   - Use the attached prompt_set_v2.jsonl without modification for A/B parity.
   - Batch size: 16. KV cache enabled. Temperature fixed to 0 for deterministic scoring.

3) A/B canary plan (ops)
   - Week 0 (canary start, target May 17): 5% traffic (search only, US).
   - If metrics stable after 72h: 20% for 4 days.
   - If stable: 100% after day 10.
   - Automatic rollback triggers: NDCG@10 drop > 1.0 pts OR MRR down > 2.5% relative to baseline over 24h window.

4) Monitoring & regression detection
   - We will surface token-level latency, per-route NDCG/MRR, and example-level quality flags in the Redwood Console.
   - Suggest an agreement to hold the baseline model for at least 48h before full cutover to monitor for unseen regressions on long-tail queries.

5) Post-mortem / evaluation artifacts
   - We’ll export a per-query diff table and a small stratified review set (100 queries) for human review if the Canary shows any anomalies.

Next steps for scheduling: Sergio, can you confirm Redwood’s availability for a 30-min kickoff the week of May 10 to finalize gating rules and dashboard access? Emily, if May 17 start is firm on your end we’ll prioritize dev time.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Applied ML
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: evaluation pack & A/B schedule for rerank validation

Marissa / Sergio —

This looks good. Confirming:
- We’ll start the canary on May 17 (US search only).
- Start traffic pattern: 5% → 20% (if stable) → 100% as described.
- Agree to the rollback gates; please make the threshold conservative (use the values Marissa suggested).

We would like Redwood to grant dashboard access to our analytics lead (Amit Rao) and to get the per-query diff export daily during the canary.

Sergio — please send a calendar invite for a 30-min kickoff (May 11 or 12 preferred). Also attaching the signed mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_Shopline_May2027.pdf) — please countersign when you have a moment.

Thanks,
Emily

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_Shopline_May2027.pdf (application/pdf)
